quarterly_data.signal: R&D and corporate events: R&D spend H1 KRW 84,267M (22.09% of revenue, vs 18.41% in FY2025), all expensed; patents 1,188 registered / 847 pending (122 patents granted in H1 2026 across Korea, US, China, Taiwan, Japan, including tungsten nucleation-layer, dielectric-film and gap-fill methods). Product line: CVD (GEMINI, QUARTO, LEVATA), ALD (HYETA, GEMINI, PRESTO, CLARO, VELOCE), metal deposition (NOA), thermal (300 SERIES, MODUS) for DRAM, NAND and logic; display dry etch, PI cure, LTPS furnace and low-temperature PECVD for thin-film encapsulation (localising a process currently supplied by a single foreign vendor). Active R&D projects at 2026-06-30 include: isotropic dry selective-removal process for next-generation 3D NAND; PVD system for 2um-class panel-level (500x500mm+) RDL seed layers (panel-level packaging); induction-heating wafer heating cutting electricity 25%+; 3D-printed gas injector for deposition tools; 8.6-generation high-density plasma CVD and dry-etch systems for IT OLED. Completed Q4 2025: very-high-frequency PECVD oxide/nitride stack deposition tool for next-generation VNAND; in-vacuo XPS ALE research; stable power supply and fast impedance matching for system-semiconductor deposition tools. Governance: Kim Yong-gil (former Applied Materials Korea and ASM Korea chairman) elected inside director and board chair on 2026-03-24; charter amended 2026-03-24 (independent-director ratio, director duty of loyalty to shareholders, quarterly dividend clause); board on 2026-07-24 approved a plan to retain all 428,211 treasury shares (0.87%) as employee stock compensation, up to 80,000 shares to be granted before the 2027 AGM (53,000 planned in 2026), subject to an extraordinary general meeting on 2026-09-04, which will also vote on Choi Geun-min (former SK On CPO, SK Siltron, SK Hynix production-technology centre head) as a new independent director. Credit rating A+ (eCredible, 2026-05-04), cash-flow grade upgraded to A from B. Auditor changed to Ernst & Young Han Young for 2026-2028. Committed KRW 14,400M (31.1%) to DTS No.1 private equity fund (formed 2026-01-23; KRW 14,105M paid). Share price rose from a January 2026 low of KRW 73,300 to a June 2026 high of KRW 183,300.

quarterly_data.signal: AI / HBM framing in the half-year report (2026-08-14): the memory market is leading semiconductor growth on AI and big-data demand, and the equipment market is expected to keep growing over the medium-to-long term on the aggressive DRAM-centric investment memory makers are making to break the HBM SHORTAGE caused by the explosive expansion of AI end-markets. 2022-2024 is described as a harsh down-cycle (memory price collapse, utilisation drop); 2025-2030 is framed as a structural growth phase driven by generative-AI infrastructure build-out, led by HBM and sub-2nm foundry rather than commodity products. The AI-accelerator and HBM demand surge is forcing the equipment market onto a single high-end track where marginal technology or adequate tools have no place; foreign vendors from the US, Japan and Netherlands still hold the largest shares but Korean localisation is rising and the company's tools are now in mass-production lines of major customers at home and abroad, with overseas sales rising (China semiconductor revenue KRW 63,346M in H1 2026 vs KRW 42,017M in H1 2025). Company cannot estimate market share because device makers' total orders are not observable.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM shortage-driven DRAM capex cited as multi-year equipment driver; 2025-2030 structural growth phase (HBM, sub-2nm foundry)
